title: CT Perfusion improves Detection and Exclusion of Clinically Relevant Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusions - A Multi-Reader Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
justification: The study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of CT perfusion in detecting DMVOs using a retrospective design with paired-reader assessments, which fits the criteria for a cohort study.

title: Autophagy in ischemic stroke: pathophysiology, therapeutics, and challenges ahead.
cebm_label: Case report, case series, expert opinion, animal study, or in-vitro study
justification: The paper is a narrative review synthesizing preclinical and emerging clinical evidence rather than presenting original research data or a systematic review of RCTs. It does not provide a specific sample size as it discusses various studies and concepts.

title: Efficacy and Safety of an Early Aggressive Lipid-Lowering Strategy Using Triple Therapy After Mechanical Thrombectomy.
justification: The study is a retrospective analysis of patients classified into two treatment groups, which fits the definition of a cohort study. It does not involve randomization, thus it cannot be classified as an RCT.

title: Risk prediction of traumatic and non-traumatic subdural hematoma after ischemic stroke: a nationwide competing-risk model with external validation.
justification: The study is a nationwide retrospective cohort analysis using health insurance data, which fits the criteria for a cohort study. It examines the risk factors for subdural hematoma in ischemic stroke survivors over a large sample size.

title: Clinical effect of kinesio taping combined with dry needling to myofascial trigger point on shoulder-hand syndrome in hemiplegia patients: a randomized controlled trial.
justification: The study is a prospective, double-blind randomized controlled trial with a clearly defined intervention and control groups, making it an individual RCT. The sample size of 84 participants is explicitly mentioned.

title: Comparison of KAFO and AFO for extension thrust pattern after stroke: a randomized N-of-1 trial.
cebm_label: Case report, case series, expert opinion, animal study, or in-vitro study
justification: This study is an N-of-1 trial involving a single participant, which does not meet the criteria for higher levels of evidence such as randomized controlled trials or cohort studies. Therefore, it is classified as a case report.

title: Delayed M1 Dissection After Thrombectomy Treated With Rescue Stenting and Tirofiban: A Case Report.
cebm_label: Case report, case series, expert opinion, animal study, or in-vitro study
justification: This study describes a single case of delayed M1 dissection after thrombectomy, which is characteristic of a case report. There are no comparisons or controls, and it does not involve a systematic review or trial.

title: Assessing efficacy and safety of dynamic scalp acupuncture for post-stroke rehabilitation: systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
cebm_label: Systematic review or meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs)
justification: The paper outlines a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, which is considered the highest level of evidence in the CEBM hierarchy. However, the actual sample size will be determined during the review process and is not specified in the abstract.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Strategies Defined by Drug Composition and Treatment Duration for Acute Minor Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk Transient Ischemic Attack: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

study_design: Systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
justification: The study is a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes data from multiple randomized controlled trials, which is the highest level of evidence in the CEBM hierarchy.

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Minimally Invasive Surgery for Infratentorial Hemorrhages: A Meta-Analysis of Clinical and Technical Outcomes.
cebm_label: Systematic review or meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs)
justification: The paper is a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes data from multiple studies, which is the highest level of evidence. However, it does not specify if the included studies were RCTs, which is necessary for a Level 1 classification.

title: The association between social support and quality of life in patients with severe stroke: a chain mediation analysis of resilience and self-efficacy.
justification: The study is a cross-sectional observational study that examines associations between variables rather than establishing causation, fitting the criteria for a cohort study level. It does not involve randomization or control groups typical of higher-level evidence.

sample_size: n=604 (302 in each group after matching)
justification: The study is a retrospective cohort analysis using propensity score matching to compare outcomes between two treatment groups, which fits the criteria for a cohort study rather than a randomized controlled trial.

title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study.
sample_size: n=1055 (group A), n=721 (group B), n=144 (group C), n=161 (group D)
justification: The study involves the evaluation of a multiagent large language model framework using both retrospective and prospective cases, which fits the definition of a cohort study. It assesses treatment recommendations and decision-making accuracy among physicians, but does not involve randomization.

title: Diagnostic value of cardiovascular biomarkers for cerebral-cardiac syndrome risk in acute ischemic stroke.
justification: The study analyzes data from a cohort of patients with acute ischemic stroke to identify risk factors for cerebral-cardiac syndrome, which fits the criteria for a cohort study. It is not a randomized controlled trial or a systematic review.

title: Sex Disparities in Enrollment in Recent Randomized Clinical Trials of Acute Stroke: A Meta-analysis.
cebm_label: Systematic review or meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs)
justification: The study is a meta-analysis that synthesizes data from multiple randomized clinical trials to assess sex disparities in enrollment, which qualifies it as a systematic review of RCTs.

title: The Efficacy of the proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) approach in stroke rehabilitation to improve basic activities of daily living and quality of life: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
